newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stressed sales rise in 95/96 - report.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stressed sales rise in 95/96 - report.

text.p: Sales of financially troubled businesses in Australia rose for the first time in six years after a surge in such sales during the June quarter, accountants Ernst & Young said on Monday.
Their 1995/96 Business Stress Index, which measures the incidence of so-called "stress sales" advertised nationally, showed a six percent rise to 202 in 1995/96 from 191 a year earlier.
Stress sales in the June quarter numbered 72, up from 38 in the June quarter of 1995 and corresponding with an increase in insolvency work, the accountants said.

"The findings...reinforce our experience in the marketplace. There has been more insolvency work over the past few months and the trend has continued into the new financial year," Ernst & Young partner Michael Scales said in a statement.
The number of stress sales in the manufacturing sector continued to dominate the national total, despite falling slightly to 66 in 95/96.
Agriculture stress sales jumped 83 percent reflecting the continuing weakness in wool prices and a recent sharp fall in domestic beef prices, Ernst & Young director of agribusines Geoff James said.
The trend in the storage and transport sector fared worst, with stress sales over the year leaping 320 percent to 21.
